milestone.title: raul configurable keybinds via ~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml — TUI-wide keymap with sane defaults

intent.outcome: Every raul lane's key-binding is read from a per-user TOML config (`~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml`) at startup, with the existing hardcoded values as defaults when the file is absent. The user can remap any keybind without rebuilding raul. Existing keyboard paths stay canonical; the config is additive.

problem.description: All keybinds are hardcoded in each lane's app.rs / keybinds.rs. Remapping (e.g. `<space>` pause on the autopilot lane → `<F1>`) requires rebuilding raul and reinstalling. The M198 follow-on (Settings 2.0) shipped a typed config schema for `ui.*` values but did not extend to keymaps. This milestone adds the config surface for keymaps, plumbs it into the existing keybind dispatch in each lane, and surfaces a Settings affordance to view/edit the current keymap.

in_scope: Define `crates/raul/src/tui/keybinds.rs::Keybinds` (or extend the existing module) to load `~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml` at startup with the schema: each lane's section (e.g. `[autopilot]`, `[milestones]`) maps action names (e.g. `pause`, `cancel`, `refresh`) to keyboard codes (e.g. `"<space>"`, `"<F1>"`, `"r"`).
Default values for every keybind are stored in code; the TOML only overrides.

Per-lane loading: each lane's app.rs reads its section at construction time; an unknown action in the TOML is ignored (with a one-line warning on stderr); an unparseable key string is treated as the default.

Live reload via SIGHUP: a running raul instance re-reads the TOML when it receives SIGHUP; the change applies on the next input cycle. (Reload is non-blocking — failures degrade silently to the previous keymap.)
Settings lane exposes the active keymap as a read-only view (per the M198 precedent); edits happen in the user's TOML, not in-app.
Cross-platform: keyboard strings use ratatui's KeyCode display (`"<space>"`, `"<F1>"`, `"<Enter>"`); the parser handles the same set as ratatui accepts.
out_of_scope: In-app keymap editor (Settings lane surfaces the active map; editing happens externally).
Mouse bindings (M221's mouse handler is a separate surface; keybinds.toml is keyboard-only).

Per-role keybinds inside the autopilot tab (e.g. `<space>` for orchestrator vs `<space>` for runner). The autopilot tab's existing per-role keymap is unchanged; the TOML applies to the lane as a whole.
Backwards-incompatible default changes (defaults preserve current behavior; the TOML is opt-in).

acceptance_criteria.description: At startup, each lane loads its section from `~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml`. When the file is absent, every lane uses its hardcoded default keymap; behavior unchanged. Verified by running the full raul regression without the file present.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Adding a `[autopilot] pause = "<F1>"` line to the TOML causes the autopilot lane to respond to `<F1>` instead of `<space>` on the next input cycle. Verified by a fixture that drops a TOML with a custom autoparallel pause key and asserts the lane's dispatch calls accept `<F1>` and reject `<space>`.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Unknown actions in the TOML are ignored (with a stderr warning); unparseable key strings fall back to the default. Verified by a fixture that injects both kinds of bad entries and asserts the warning + the lane still uses defaults for those actions.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: SIGHUP reload: sending SIGHUP to a running raul causes the keymap to be reloaded from disk on the next input cycle. A test that writes a new TOML, sends SIGHUP (via a child-process helper), and asserts the new keymap is live in <100ms.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Settings lane exposes the active keymap as a read-only view per lane (per M198 precedent). Edits happen externally in the user's TOML, not in-app.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: opening Settings shows the current keymap per lane; verified against a representative TOML with overrides in `~/.config/raul/keybinds.toml`.

design_decisions.choice: TOML section per lane, action-name → key-code strings, default values live in code (not in a default-file).
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids the 'defaults drift from code' problem; the source-of-truth for defaults is the code, and the TOML is opt-in overrides.

design_decisions.choice: SIGHUP triggers reload (not inotify) because SIGHUP works on every platform (macOS, Linux, BSD) and is one signal; inotify would need a platform-specific watcher.
design_decisions.rationale: Cross-platform portability with one signal; the user can `killall -HUP raul` (or use the harness's hook) to reload.

design_decisions.choice: Unknown actions ignored + warn; unparseable key strings fall back to defaults. No abort on bad TOML.
design_decisions.rationale: A user typo shouldn't lock the user out of the app; defaults survive errors.

work_packages.name: Configurable keymap (TUI-wide)
work_packages.goal: TOML keymap config loads at startup; each lane reads its section; SIGHUP triggers live reload; Settings shows the active map.
work_packages.rollback: Revert keybinds.toml loading to a no-op; full regression stays green.
